description: Joe chose option A on 2026-07-30: carry findings across a legacy migration rather than migrate them separately or accept the loss. Two problems today. (1) restore_legacy (src/todo_db/database.py:463) validates only its 12 required tracker tables and IGNORES every other key, then rebuilds from base=self.export() with items/events/tracker_tables overwritten. Findings never transfer, and a snapshot that DID carry them would be accepted while silently discarding them - a migration that reports success and loses a domain. (2) Carrying them is not just an importer change: this package's findings STORAGE is a version behind BenchBox's. Migrations stop at 004_findings.sql (the v3 shape); related_paths and suggested_sweep appear only as recognized draft-payload keys in findings.py:51, not as columns; and finding_sections does not exist. BenchBox's v4 (todo_findings.finding_migration_v4_statements) adds findings.related_paths, findings.suggested_sweep and the finding_sections table, and recreates finding_links. So a migration must land here before the importer can be lossless. Upstream context: BenchBox PR #1354 added 'todo export --snapshot FILE' producing the 12-table normalized dump restore-legacy consumes; this item is what lets that dump also carry findings.

work_units.evidence: Added migrations/005_findings_lossless.sql mirroring BenchBox's finding_migration_v4_statements(): findings.related_paths, findings.suggested_sweep, the finding_sections table with UNIQUE(finding_id, position) and its index, and a finding_links rebuild so target_item's FK to items(id) is DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED - a restore loads tables one at a time, so a finding can reference an item that does not exist yet. Bumped SCHEMA_VERSION 4 -> 5. Verified on a fresh DB: 'schema v5 ready', findings has both new columns, all five finding tables exist, finding_links target_item is deferrable.
work_units.summary: Add migration 005 bringing findings storage to BenchBox v4 (related_paths, suggested_sweep, finding_sections)

work_units.evidence: restore_legacy now rejects tables it cannot load instead of ignoring them. Added OPTIONAL_LEGACY_TABLES (the five findings tables) and a check that anything in neither the required nor optional set raises SchemaMismatchError naming the offenders. Verified against a real 1683-item BenchBox snapshot: the unmodified snapshot still restores, and the same snapshot with an injected 'some_future_table' is refused with 'legacy snapshot carries tables this importer cannot load: some_future_table'. A test also asserts the refusal leaves the destination byte-identical (export() before == after).
work_units.summary: Make restore_legacy reject unknown tables instead of ignoring them

work_units.evidence: restore_legacy now copies the five findings tables from the snapshot, using the same .get(table, []) semantics as the required tables so --replace means replace: an absent findings table becomes empty rather than leaving destination rows, which would otherwise produce a hybrid of two trackers. Adding a table turned out to need FOUR independent lists, not one - and the first attempt missed two of them. finding_sections restored 0 rows while the other four restored 1, despite the restore reporting success and audit verify passing; only counting rows caught it. The four places: restore_legacy's copy loop, restore()'s table_columns (needed related_paths/suggested_sweep on findings plus a finding_sections entry), restore()'s insert_order and delete_order, and export()'s per-table SELECT map - which also lacked finding_sections, so sections would have silently vanished on any re-export.
work_units.summary: Extend restore_legacy to load the five findings tables

work_units.evidence: Round-tripped a real snapshot of the live BenchBox tracker (1683 items, 4187 events) with findings injected into all five tables, restored into a scratch SQLite DB - never the hosted DB. All five tables land with the expected row counts, related_paths and suggested_sweep survive verbatim, the finding_sections body survives, and audit verify still returns a valid chain of 4187 events. Three unit tests pin it: findings carried (all five tables + lossless fields + section text + chain intact), unknown table rejected with the destination untouched, and a 12-table snapshot without findings still restoring (findings optional, not newly required). Suite 102 passed, ruff clean. Kept the diff isolated: 'ruff format src tests' reformatted five files I never touched, so those were reverted and only my own long line was wrapped.
work_units.summary: Round-trip a real BenchBox snapshot and confirm findings survive with audit verify clean
